Author: @ashleevance | Text: It's been about 18 months since fires destroyed homes in the Palisades. Rebuilding has gone slowly thanks to insurance companies, regulations and a lack of labor. 

The very first total rebuild came via an unlikely player - Cover. 

It does prefab but not prefab like you know it. The homes are made of metal and have high-end finishings, and they can go up in about a month to 45 days. 

Cover has its work ahead of it trying to take on the California housing market. Bu
viral_opportunities.author: @ashleevance
viral_opportunities.summary: Ashlee Vance tweet on 18-month-slow Palisades rebuild, blaming insurers, regulation, and labor shortage.
viral_opportunities.engagement_angle: Palisades rebuild-pace story without design/insurance-reform hook; monitor for a design-forward rebuttal angle.

viral_reply.body: Speed matters, but so does what underwriters see — non-combustible assemblies are one of the few levers that actually move insurability in the Palisades rebuild math.

Author: @BridgetAyers | Text: I might be mistaken but...

While Jonathan Scott’s RSG 3-D system uses components classified as non-combustible (meaning they will not ignite, feed, or spread the flames), the house itself can absolutely still fail if exposed to extreme, sustained heat. No residential material is entirely immune to destruction in a high-intensity firestorm.

viral_opportunities.author: @BridgetAyers
viral_opportunities.summary: X thread questioning the non-combustible classification of Jonathan Scott's RSG 3-D fireproofing system.
viral_opportunities.engagement_angle: Offer technical substance on real non-combustible reinforced-concrete assemblies vs. marketed 'fire-resistant' systems.

viral_reply.body: Fair read — the honest framing is performance, not immunity. Shotcrete over the panel keeps flame off the structure, and that's what underwriters actually score.
